title: No One's Crazy
coreMove: Translate a strange money choice back into the life that made it feel sensible.
sourcePressure: Different financial histories make risk, reward, and fear feel different, so behavior that looks irrational from outside can be coherent from inside.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Explaining every disagreement as stupidity, ignorance, or lack of discipline.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening No One's Crazy with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
counterintuition: reducing No One's Crazy to common-sense advice
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the money history move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of money history and inflation memory

exampleSpecs.domain: a coastal town insurance office after three storm evacuations in five years
exampleSpecs.audience: an agent explaining why one family over-insures while another gambles
exampleSpecs.stakes: misjudging clients as irrational will lose both policies and trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the agent asks each spouse to point to the storm that taught them what safe means before recommending coverage
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a flood map pinned beside two damp cardboard claim folders

exampleSpecs.domain: a first-generation college financial aid desk during award-letter week
exampleSpecs.audience: a counselor hearing why debt feels different across households
exampleSpecs.stakes: one student may decline a good loan because family memory treats debt as danger
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the counselor stops explaining interest rates and asks who in the family still talks about the repossessed van
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a financial aid letter folded into quarters inside a backpack pocket

exampleSpecs.domain: a used camera shop negotiating trade-ins with retired newspaper photographers and teen creators
exampleSpecs.audience: a shop owner managing two groups who value equipment differently
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same price feels insulting or generous depending on the era that trained the buyer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner writes each customer's first paid camera year on the appraisal sheet before discussing value
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glass case reflecting an old Nikon beside a phone rig

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood grocery co-op debating bulk-buy rules after inflation spikes
exampleSpecs.audience: a board chair trying to decode hoarding without shaming members
exampleSpecs.stakes: strict limits may punish members whose childhood scarcity makes shelves feel unsafe
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair asks members to mark which price jump changed their pantry habits before setting limits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pallet of rice sacks next to handwritten purchase-limit signs

exampleSpecs.domain: a public library fine-forgiveness program meeting resistance from older trustees
exampleSpecs.audience: a library director explaining that fines mean responsibility to one generation and exclusion to another
exampleSpecs.stakes: a policy vote could close access for families the library wants back
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after low turnout, the director maps trustees' first library memories against patrons' current bus costs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a checkout desk drawer filled with expired library cards

exampleSpecs.domain: a community theater splitting ticket revenue between veteran actors and new livestream crew
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer mediating people shaped by different career markets
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fair formula collapses if each side thinks the other is playing the same game
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the producer has each side state what a paid gig meant in their first working year before numbers are negotiated
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rehearsal hall floor taped for blocking beside a laptop on a tripod
